remediation.defect: generate_contracts.py's $ref resolution (rsplit('/')[-1] then _safe_name) never applied the Gateway/Memory prefix _models() itself adds to OpenAPI object records, and had no path at all for $ref targets that are not object records. Every field referencing another Gateway/Memory-prefixed model, or a scalar/array alias component, or a whole-document forwarding alias, silently emitted a name nothing declares. Undetected since OCOR-DEV-0010's own test suite only asserts each model's own declaration line is present, never that the file as a whole resolves or compiles.
remediation.discovery: The very first real `tsc --strict` compile of the generator's own output, prompted by DEC-212 Phase 2.3's requirement that the TypeScript SDK actually compile rather than merely be emitted as text -- exactly the gap OCOR_LANGUAGE_POLICY.md's row 7 already named as the open risk.
remediation.fix_scope: ocor-runtime/tools/generate_contracts.py only (a new _build_reference_index() function plus wiring _schema_type/_schema_model to consume it); PINNED_GENERATED_HASHES updated to match. The sealed ocor-runtime/tests/tasks/test_ocor_dev_0010.py is untouched and its full suite re-verified green. Model inventory (54 models, same names) unchanged -- only cross-reference resolution correctness changed.

note: Phase 2.3 of mandate CC-LANGUAGE-POLICY-AND-GAP-CLOSURE: a real TypeScript SDK under ocor-runtime/sdk/typescript, generated by the existing generator (never hand-written -- the generated ocor_contracts.ts is byte-identical to a fresh `generate_contracts.py generate` run, verified mechanically by both new test suites), with tsconfig strict, tsc==7.0.2 compilation wired into the type-and-lint-gate CI job, and the NFR-022 cross-SDK conformance suite proving canonical-byte/digest/error-model/idempotency-binding identity between the Python kernel and the compiled TypeScript SDK on shared fixtures.
